outcome: No proof, disproof or verified reduction of Dade's conjecture in any of its forms has been posted since 26 January 2024 that I could find. The window holds one reduction (Rossi, February 2024) of Späth's Character Triple Conjecture to its quasi-simple case, which leaves Dade's conjecture open, and neighbouring results (McKay, Alperin–McKay for p = 2, the Eaton–Moretó conjecture on principal blocks, Alperin weight-type results) that do not settle it; one of these (Arranz, Gómez-Serrano, Navarro, Schaeffer Fry, August 2026) credits AI systems with load-bearing proof steps on the neighbouring conjecture.
problem_asks: Read from the statement alone: (1) for a finite group G and a prime p, and for the blocks of G, a counting identity relating the numbers of irreducible characters in blocks of G to the corresponding numbers for blocks of the local subgroups of G; (2) that identity holds for every finite group G and every prime p (the statement is universal, so a single failing group or prime would be a counterexample); (3) the statement names no particular form of the identity (no defect, no ordinary or projective refinement, no inductive condition), so the form the problem asks for is what the literature calls Dade's conjecture, which has ordinary, projective and inductive versions. Nothing in the statement asks about the Alperin–McKay, McKay, Alperin weight or Brauer height zero conjectures, which are consequences or neighbours and not parts of the problem.

events.what_happened: Damiano Rossi, ‘A reduction theorem for the Character Triple Conjecture’, arXiv:2402.10632 (math.RT, math.GR). The Character Triple Conjecture (CTC) is Späth’s strengthening of Dade’s projective conjecture. Theorem A (arXiv v2 wording): if the CTC holds at a prime p for every covering group of every non-abelian simple group involved in G, then it holds for G at p. The abstract says the CTC holds for all finite groups once assumed for all quasi-simple groups, and that this answers the question of a self-reducing form of Dade’s conjecture; the introduction says the CTC is the right candidate for that form and that the reduction ‘will play an active role in the final proof of Dade’s Conjecture’, which it treats as future work. The paper does not claim to prove Dade’s conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 16 Feb 2024; v2 26 Feb 2024 (the current arXiv version). A search-index listing gives the journal as Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society 2025, doi 10.1112/plms.70090; the Wiley page returned HTTP 403, so that publication is unverified.
events.delivers: Theorem A: the CTC for all finite groups at p, given the CTC for covering groups of the non-abelian simple groups involved. A cancellation theorem for the CTC is also stated (its statement, Theorem 5.2, was not read). It is a reduction: it moves the CTC from ‘all finite groups’ to ‘covering groups of non-abelian simple groups’. It does not prove the CTC for any quasi-simple group, and it proves nothing about Dade’s ordinary conjecture. Via Späth (2017), the CTC implies Dade’s projective conjecture, so the reduction bears on that form only conditionally.
events.remains: The whole statement: the CTC for covering groups of non-abelian simple groups is still needed; Dade’s ordinary and inductive forms are not addressed; the identity for all finite groups is not established for any form.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (Wiley)
checked_by.what_they_did: Publication listed in a search index as Proc. LMS 2025, doi 10.1112/plms.70090. The page could not be opened (HTTP 403), so acceptance is unverified.

events.direction: Cuts toward Dade’s projective-type statements (the CTC implies Dade’s projective conjecture by Späth 2017), but as a reduction to an open hypothesis. It neither asserts nor refutes any form of Dade’s conjecture.

events.what_happened: Asier Arranz, Javier Gómez-Serrano, Gabriel Navarro, A. A. Schaeffer Fry, ‘On The Eaton-Moretó Conjecture for Principal Blocks of Finite Groups’, arXiv:2608.16398 (math.RT, math.GR). Theorem A: for a finite group G with non-abelian Sylow p-subgroup P, the principal p-block of G contains an irreducible character χ with 1 < χ(1)ₚ ≤ m(P), where m(P) is the smallest non-linear irreducible degree of P. Corollary B: if Dade’s projective conjecture holds for the principal block of G, then the full Eaton–Moretó conjecture holds for that block. The acknowledgements (arXiv HTML v1) say the paper grew out of a Navarro–Gómez-Serrano conversation, that AI produced a proof of a weaker block-free version of Theorem A, and that with further AI help the authors proved Theorem A; they say the final proof was simplified and revised and is written entirely by them.
events.revisions: v1 17 Aug 2026; the arXiv abstract page lists one version only.
events.delivers: Unconditionally, the existence of a character χ in the principal block with 1 < χ(1)ₚ ≤ m(P) (one of the two inequalities of the Eaton–Moretó conjecture for principal blocks, for groups with non-abelian Sylow p-subgroups). The reverse inequality, and so the full principal-block Eaton–Moretó conjecture, is conditional on Dade’s projective conjecture for the principal block. Restriction: principal blocks only, and only the one inequality is proved.
events.remains: Dade’s conjecture entirely: the paper does not prove or assume it outside Corollary B. For the Eaton–Moretó conjecture, the reverse inequality remains (it follows only if Dade’s projective conjecture holds for the principal block).
events.time_since_posted: about 8 weeks to October 2026; I did not find any public commentary in my searches
events.direction: Cuts for the Eaton–Moretó conjecture (it proves one inequality for principal blocks) and is consistent with Dade’s projective conjecture, which the paper assumes only for the converse. It does not touch whether Dade’s conjecture holds.

events.what_happened: Marc Cabanes and Britta Späth, ‘The McKay Conjecture on character degrees’, arXiv:2410.20392. Proves McKay’s conjecture (for every prime ℓ, the groups G and N_G(P) for a Sylow ℓ-subgroup P have equally many irreducible characters of degree prime to ℓ) for all finite groups, using the classification of finite simple groups. The arXiv page says ‘to appear in Annals of Mathematics’. Dade’s conjecture is not mentioned in the abstract.
events.delivers: McKay’s conjecture for all finite groups and all primes. McKay’s conjecture is a consequence of Dade’s conjecture, not the conjecture itself, so this does not settle Dade’s conjecture in any form.
events.remains: All of the problem: the block-level identity for every finite group, in each of Dade’s ordinary, projective and inductive forms.

checked_by.who: Annals of Mathematics (per the arXiv comment ‘to appear’)
checked_by.what_they_did: Acceptance indicated only by the arXiv comment; not verified against the journal

events.direction: Confirms a conjecture that Dade’s conjecture implies (McKay). It is about McKay’s conjecture and says nothing about whether Dade’s conjecture holds.

events.what_happened: Alexander Moretó, ‘Alperin’s Main Problem of Block Theory’, arXiv:2605.11988 (math.RT, math.GR). Proposes a conjectural framework for Alperin’s 1976 Main Problem, using the sets Irr^x(G) of characters not vanishing at an element x and the subnormalizer Sub_G(x), and says McKay’s conjecture is recovered at degree level. It claims to verify its own main conjectures in several families (including simple groups with TI Sylow p-subgroups). Dade’s conjecture is not mentioned in the visible abstract.
events.revisions: v1 12 May 2026; v2 21 May 2026; v3 1 Jun 2026 (listed as minor changes).
events.delivers: A new conjectural framework for Alperin’s Main Problem, with checks in named families. It is not a settlement of Alperin’s Main Problem as posed, and it does not address Dade’s conjecture.
events.remains: All of Dade’s conjecture; the author’s framework is itself conjectural in general.
events.time_since_posted: about 5 months; I did not search for commentary on it specifically
events.direction: Proposes a framework and families of verifications; neither confirms nor refutes Dade’s conjecture or any stated conjecture in the problem.

events.what_happened: Zhicheng Feng, J. Miquel Martínez, Damiano Rossi, ‘Alperin’s bound and normal Sylow subgroups’, arXiv:2502.12841. Reduces the Malle–Navarro–Tiep conjecture (equal numbers of p-Brauer characters for G and N_G(P) iff P normal) to finite simple groups for general p and proves it for p = 2, and reduces the blockwise Alperin lower bound on p-Brauer characters to a simpler case, proving it for 2-blocks of maximal defect.
events.delivers: The Malle–Navarro–Tiep conjecture for p = 2, and a reduction of the Malle–Navarro–Tiep conjecture for general p to simple groups; the blockwise Alperin lower bound for maximal-defect 2-blocks. Neither is Dade’s conjecture, which the page does not mention.
events.remains: Dade’s conjecture entirely; the Malle–Navarro–Tiep conjecture for odd p; the blockwise bound for other blocks.
events.time_since_posted: about 20 months; I did not search for commentary on it specifically
events.direction: Proves neighbouring cases of different conjectures (Malle–Navarro–Tiep, Alperin’s bound). It does not bear on whether Dade’s conjecture holds.

events.what_happened: Baoyu Zhang, ‘On the inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition for type B and type C’, arXiv:2609.24774 (math.GR, math.RT). Proves the inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition for finite simple groups of types B and C at every prime dividing their order, and for the sporadic groups J4, Fi′24, the Baby Monster and the Monster. The abstract says that with earlier results this implies the blockwise Alperin weight conjecture for groups whose non-abelian simple sections of order divisible by ℓ are of type B, C or sporadic. The PDF comments field says: ‘For information on the Lean sources and reflections on the use of AI in mathematical research please see the acknowledgements.’ The author notes that the CTBlocks GAP package still listed these four sporadic verifications as incomplete on 19 September 2026.
events.delivers: Inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition for types B and C and four sporadic groups. The Alperin weight conjecture is a neighbour of Dade’s conjecture, not Dade’s conjecture itself, so this bears on Dade only indirectly.
events.remains: Dade’s conjecture entirely; the inductive condition for other simple types; the blockwise Alperin weight conjecture for groups with other simple sections.
events.direction: Cuts for the Alperin weight condition in the stated families; no bearing on whether Dade’s conjecture holds.

events.what_happened: Britta Späth, J. Eur. Math. Soc. 19 (2017), ‘A reduction theorem for Dade’s projective conjecture’. Introduces the Character Triple Conjecture as a strengthening of Dade’s conjecture and shows that the CTC for quasi-simple groups implies Dade’s projective conjecture for all finite groups (per search snippets; not opened).
events.delivers: Conditional reduction: CTC for quasi-simple groups implies Dade’s projective conjecture for all finite groups. The ordinary conjecture is not addressed.
events.remains: The quasi-simple CTC; Dade’s projective conjecture unconditionally; Dade’s ordinary and inductive forms.

events.what_happened: Everett C. Dade, ‘Counting characters in blocks. I’, Inventiones Mathematicae 109 (1992), 187–210 (DOI 10.1007/BF01232023). States the ordinary conjecture: for a block of positive defect with trivial p-core, the number of irreducible characters of fixed defect is an alternating sum over the corresponding numbers for normalisers of non-trivial p-chains. Verified for blocks with cyclic defect groups and all blocks of M11 and J1 (per a MaRDI review snippet; not opened). Dade notes the formula can fail if O_p(G) ≠ 1 or the block has defect zero, and conjectures it otherwise.

summary: Dade’s conjecture is still open in every form I could find. The main in-window item on its core is Rossi’s preprint (arXiv:2402.10632, first posted 16 February 2024; v2 26 February 2024), which I read through its Theorem A and acknowledgements in the HTML v2 text (up to about 300,000 of 353,000 characters). Theorem A says the Character Triple Conjecture holds for G at p if it holds for covering groups of the non-abelian simple groups involved in G. This is a reduction. Späth (2017) had already shown that the CTC for quasi-simple groups would give Dade’s projective conjecture, so the 2024 result moves the hypothesis from all groups to quasi-simple groups and proves nothing about the conjecture itself. Rossi calls the CTC the right candidate for a self-reducing form of Dade’s conjecture and treats the final proof as future work. I could not verify the Proc. LMS 2025 publication, because the Wiley page returned HTTP 403, and the journal listing comes from a search index only. Close call: whether a reduction of this kind counts as moving a quantity the problem asks for. My reading is that it does not settle any part of the statement, because the reduced hypothesis is open. The other close call is the 2026 Arranz–Gómez-Serrano–Navarro–Schaeffer Fry preprint (arXiv:2608.16398, 17 August 2026). It proves one inequality for the Eaton–Moretó conjecture on principal blocks, and says that Dade’s projective conjecture would give the other. Its acknowledgements, read in the HTML v1 text, say that AI produced a proof of a weaker block-free version of Theorem A and gave further help on Theorem A, and they name the models as ChatGPT-5.6-Sol and Claude Fable 5 in a workflow the human authors ran; they say the final proof was revised by them and written entirely by them. This is load-bearing AI involvement on a neighbouring conjecture. It is not a claim about Dade’s conjecture, and the authors do not make one. The PDF did not decode, so the AI account rests on the HTML acknowledgements. Other in-window items are neighbours that do not settle the problem: Cabanes–Späth’s proof of McKay’s conjecture (27 October 2024; McKay is a consequence of Dade, not Dade); Feng–Martínez–Rossi on the Malle–Navarro–Tiep conjecture (February 2025); Zhang’s inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition for types B and C (21 September 2026), whose PDF comments point to an acknowledgements section on AI use that I could not reach; and Moretó’s framework for Alperin’s Main Problem (May 2026), which does not mention Dade. For the AI sweep I searched the problem name with AI terms, the named labs and the 2026 AI-math announcements. The OpenAI 6 October 2026 release (openai/math, 722 manuscripts in 372 families, attributed to an unreleased internal model) lists 14 group-theory results, but the index gave no titles for them, and the official announcement page returned 403. No title I could see mentions Dade, blocks, McKay or Alperin, so a block-theory entry cannot be ruled out from what I could read. Pre-2024 history (Dade 1992, 1994, 1997 announcement; Olsson–Uno 1995; An 1998; Ku 1999; An 2001; Huang 2005; An–Eaton 2005; Kessar–Linckelmann 2018; Rossi 2021, 2023; Späth 2017) verifies restricted families or implies neighbours, and none of it is a verification of the general conjecture.
competing_reading: Reading A: Rossi’s reduction, together with Späth’s 2017 result, leaves a single finite-looking task (the CTC for quasi-simple groups), so the problem is close to resolved and should count as advanced in 2024. Reading B: Arranz et al. (2026) is an AI-load-bearing mathematical result that the authors connect to Dade’s projective conjecture, so AI can be read as contributing to this problem. Against A: Theorem A is conditional on an unproven hypothesis, Rossi treats the Dade proof as future work, and the reduction does not touch the ordinary or inductive forms. Against B: the 2026 paper proves an inequality for the Eaton–Moretó conjecture and uses Dade’s projective conjecture only as an assumption for the converse; it does not claim anything about Dade’s conjecture.
what_would_settle_it: For the 2024 reduction: the Proc. LMS version (doi 10.1112/plms.70090) checked for the exact Theorem A statement and whether the quasi-simple CTC has since been proved. For Dade itself: a proof or counterexample of any of its ordinary, projective or inductive forms for all finite groups, or a proof of the quasi-simple CTC. For the 2026 AI-involved paper: the PDF or TeX source of arXiv:2608.16398 (not decoded here), and any later version stating which system produced which step. For the OpenAI release: the openai/math subject listing for the 14 group-theory entries, to rule a block-theory entry in or out. For Zhang (2609.24774): the acknowledgements section, which carries the AI reference.

judgement.why: No post-snapshot event settles or bounds any part of Dade's conjecture. Rossi 2024 is a reduction of the CTC to quasi-simple groups, an unproven condition, so it is none. The other in-window items prove different conjectures (McKay, Eaton–Moretó, Malle–Navarro–Tiep, Alperin weight, a conjectural Alperin framework), so they are variant. Arranz et al. is assisted rather than generated: the authors say AI produced a proof of a weaker block-free version and gave 'some help' with Theorem A, and that they revised and wrote the final proof themselves. It is still discarded as a variant. Zhang names no system in what was read, so it is none. The pre-snapshot verifications for restricted families (cyclic defect, symmetric groups, p-solvable groups, unitary/GL groups) are cases; McL is a single group, so it is instances.
judgement.doubts: Zhang 2609.24774's AI acknowledgements were not read, and neither were the 14 group-theory entries in the OpenAI release. Both are irrelevant to the status here because neither concerns Dade's conjecture itself. Several pre-snapshot entries rest on unopened snippets. I marked journal publications as digested on the record's word.
